evidence.verification: `/usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 8 passed in 0.01 s. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (Magnus 17.625 -> 17.27; outdoor vapour pressure computed at indoor temperature), 4 survived: the sign of the net-condensation mass balance (model.py:81, flux_in - flux_out -> flux_in + flux_out), PERM 57.2 -> 5.72 (every rate off 10x), interior film 0.12 -> 0 and kraft permeance 1 -> 10 perm (which flips the Chicago kraft result). No test pins any absolute condensation rate or any value in results.txt. test_poly_worse_than_paint_in_summer_miami_inward_drive asserts 0 >= 0 (both are zero in results.txt), and test_single_plane_mass_balance checks only non-negativity, not a mass balance.
evidence.craft: Read src/house_dewpoint/model.py (121 lines), tests/test_dewpoint.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py, pyproject.toml. Stdlib only, small pure functions, docstrings give units, deterministic, figure parses results.txt rather than retyping numbers. Defects: two test names promise more than they check (above); the 'none' retarder is a 1000-perm dummy layer so 'none' and 'paint' rows are the same wall twice (6.14 vs 6.18); condensation() returns 'rh' values above 100% (141%) under the name rh, unclamped; run.py reports RH at the OSB outer face while condensation happens at its inner face (node 2), which is what misled the headline; figure.py depends on research/_shared via a relative path; no input validation (perm 0 -> ZeroDivisionError).
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt and the independent check: headline (1), (2) numbers, (3), (5) backed; the README is unusually candid (inputs 'from memory', references 'not read in this run', Glaser not WUFI, disclaimer present). Failing: (4) 'Exterior foam alone moves the condensing plane to the sheathing face: with 1 in XPS in Chicago the sheathing's unclamped RH is 97%' is wrong: both with and without foam the only condensing node is the batt/OSB interface (node 2: 6.18 -> 2.34 g/m2/d, unclamped RH 141% -> 114%); foam does not move the plane, it warms it (-2.4 C -> 2.0 C). The 97% is the OSB's outer face, which never condenses. (2) says kraft 'removes it' while the same sentence gives 0.05 g/m2/d and table B excludes kraft+none in Chicago. Test names (mass balance, poly worse in summer) claim checks the tests do not make.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: ISO 13788 (monthly Glaser with accumulation and drying), IRC R702.7 / Table R702.7.1 (Class III retarder permitted in zone 5 on 2x6 with continuous insulation >= R-7.5, zone 7 with >= R-15), Lstiburek's dew-point / first-condensing-surface method (Building Science Corp.), ASHRAE 160 and WUFI for transient design. The model reproduces the IRC answer (Chicago: paint+R-10 XPS clean, paint+R-5 condenses; Duluth: R-10 is not enough) but does not cite it, so the 'result' is a known code table recovered with unsourced inputs, single steady months and no accumulation. Not new; the research brief's PhD/publishable bar is not approached. The kernel is correct and small, and it already graduated into ventures/wall-condensation-check (month-by-month with drying), which supersedes it for anyone building on it.
evidence.domain: Compared with ISO 13788 and ASHRAE Fundamentals ch. 25-27 practice: Glaser construction right (equals the tangent method), unit conversions right, permeances and R-values in typical ranges (painted gypsum 5 perm, kraft 1, 6-mil poly 0.06, OSB 2, XPS 1/0.5). Departures a hygrothermal engineer would hit at once: saturation over water, not ice, below 0 C; a single design month with no accumulation/drying balance, which is the ISO 13788 criterion; climates and indoor RH from memory; vented cladding counted in the thermal path; RH reported at the non-condensing face. Summer inward drive is acknowledged as uninformative.

verdict: A small, correct steady-state Glaser kernel. Its numbers reproduce byte for byte, agree within 1% with an independent IAPWS + taut-string implementation, its greedy clamp equals the tangent construction on 20,000 random walls, and its retarder/foam pattern matches the IRC R702.7 continuous-insulation table it does not cite. It misses the bar on verification (4 of 6 seeded bugs survive, including a 10x unit error and the mass-balance sign, and one test asserts 0 >= 0) and on claims (headline (4) says foam moves the condensing plane, but the model condenses at the batt/OSB interface in both cases and the 97% quoted is the other face). As research it is a known code result recovered from unsourced inputs, with saturation over water rather than ice and no ISO 13788 accumulation; the useful part has already graduated into ventures/wall-condensation-check. Finished (it does what it says), does not meet the bar.
